Lessons.Title: Graphs of Functions in Standard and Factored Forms
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: connect coefficients and factors of a quadratic expression to the horizontal and vertical intercepts of its graph, recognizing why the same function has multiple forms. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L10 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/10/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/10/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source invites students to notice patterns rather than simply memorize a sign rule.

Original function f(x)=(x−2)(x−6)=x²−8x+12. Factored form immediately gives zeros x=2 and x=6 because either factor can be zero. Standard form immediately gives y-intercept f(0)=12. The graph is an upward parabola symmetric about midpoint x=4; f(4)=(2)(−2)=−4 is its minimum.

The two representations are not two separate graphs. Check outputs at x0,2,4,6,8: 12,0,−4,0,12. At x8 the value12 agrees with symmetry about axis4. The standard-form constant term matches the y-intercept only because f(0)=c.

Student task: match three expressions to a common graph, label both intercept types, test points and propose what graphical features each form reveals most efficiently. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for equivalence, intercept reasoning, accurate graph with symmetry and articulate form-to-feature comparison.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factored zeros
KeyConcepts.Definition: A product equals zero if one factor equals zero.

KeyConcepts.Title: Standard-form y-intercept
KeyConcepts.Definition: For ax²+bx+c, at x0 output is c.
KeyConcepts.Example: For x²−8x+12 the vertical intercept is(0,12).

KeyConcepts.Title: Symmetry
KeyConcepts.Definition: For two distinct zeros, a vertical axis lies halfway between them.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Average roots for quadratic with equal-height ends.
